title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
label: J'ster

won.source: Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996): defeats Sir Giles Cavendish MP for the vacant title in a cage match, with Dark Vanity's interference again deciding the finish, this time in J'ster's favor.

how: Defended once in the held record, retaining by submission (Super J Sleeperhold) over Rick Styles on 29 Dec 1996.

title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Professor Nick Payne

won.source: Dated and described by a Deadly Draw 2 broadcast retrospective (May 1999): wins the promotion's own first Deadly Draw pay-per-view by tossing Brody Thunder over the top rope in a battle royal, at the Turning Stone Casino in upstate New York.

how: Shown vacant, in a glass case at the WrestleKade X Control Center, by the time of the card itself; no document in the held record states when or why.

won.source: Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996): defeats champion Super Destroyer.

title: dwo-1996-eastern
label: Super Destroyer

won.source: Already champion when the held record's earliest post opens; no document in the held record names how or when he won it.

how: Loses to Tommy Van Dam at Holiday Bash after a returning John Jennings, meaning to help the champion, knocks out the referee and inadvertently costs him the match.

won.source: Defeats Jeff Keenan for the vacant title at WrestleKade X.
Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996): Havok (Mr. Pink and Guy Stone) defeat The Merchants of Chaos in a Corona street fight.
Johnny Sledge and "Rodeo" Nevada Harris defeat The Riverhawks in a ladder match at WrestleKade X.

title: dwo-1996-national
label: Apollo

won.source: Already champion when the held record's earliest post opens; no document in the held record names how or when he won it.

how: Retains over Sick Rick in a steel cage at Holiday Bash, the only title match on the card not to change hands.

won.source: Already champions when the held record's earliest post opens; no document in the held record names how or when they won the titles.
Defeats Iris Galiver for the vacant title at WrestleKade X, wrestling as "Phoenix," after Samantha Bevins turns on her own hand-picked challenger.

title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Sick Rick

won.source: Wins a twenty-man Deadly Rumble battle royal for the vacant title at Deadly Draw 2, pinning Apollo last after a chair shot from DWO Owner Mike Bilodeau backfired on his own ally.

how: Loses the title in a no-disqualification match at Final Fight to a mystery challenger revealed as Jeff "Madfox" Matthews.

title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Jeff "Madfox" Matthews

won.source: Defeats champion Sick Rick in a no-disqualification match at Final Fight, the promotion's own last card, with a top-rope powerbomb.

note: The title's own next held record in the held record (WrestleKade X, 2004) finds it vacant and won again from scratch; no document in the held record states when or how this reign ended.

title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
label: "The Savior" Jamie Underwood

won.source: Wins the vacant title in the Deadly Draw Three at WrestleKade X, pinning Justin Slayne with a moonsault.

how: Held the belt after the bell only briefly: Justin Slayne and Rick Styles are shown closing the broadcast with the title belt, stolen from Underwood after his win, though no sanctioned title change followed.

title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Sir Giles Cavendish MP

won.source: Already champion when the held record's earliest post opens (30 Nov 1996); no earlier document survives naming how or when he won it.

how: J'ster won the 30 Nov 1996 cage match by a fast three-count, aided by outside interference from Dark Vanity, Razi Mahmood, Jawaad Mahmood and The Masked Man; DWO Co-President Mike Bilodeau later ruled the finish controversial and vacated the title rather than recognize either man.

title: dwo-1996-tag-team
label: The Perfectly Perfect Duo

won.source: Already billed as the reigning champions when Final Fight's own broadcast opens; no document in the held record states when or how they won the titles.

note: Retains the titles at Final Fight against the Natural Born Killers, with a manager's own botched interference nearly costing the match. The title's own next held record in the held record (WrestleKade X, 2004) finds new champions, Sledge and Harris, following an unrelated "Riverhawks" reign not otherwise documented here; no document in the held record states when or how the Perfectly Perfect Duo's own reign ended.

won.source: Final Fight (28 November 1999): wins the eight-man Thunderdome elimination match after Alex Martinez handcuffs himself to the cage rather than fall.
